Ainsley Vinall highlights a collection of photographic slides from the 1958-59 Royal Society expedition to Southern Chile, recently added to the Society's collections.
Over the last few weeks, I’ve been cataloguing a
collection of over 300 photographic slides
from the
Royal Society expedition to Southern Chile
, which took place from September 1958 to March 1959. The slides were donated in July 2024 by
Sir Martin Holdgate
(b.1931), who acted as the expedition leader. He took the vast majority himself, and donated his field notebooks, expedition diary and some objects collected during the trip.
The expedition was planned to coincide with the centenary of
On the origin of species
, the seminal work on evolutionary biology by
Charles Darwin FRS
(1809-1882) first published in 1859. Originally an extensive trip around the Southern Temperate Zone was suggested, tracking the voyage of HMS
Beagle
that took the young Darwin across this part of the world in the 1830s. However, when
HMNZS
Endeavour
, the proposed ship for this voyage, proved unavailable, the stops in Australia, New Zealand and a number of smaller islands were cut, shifting the expedition to a detailed study of Southern Chile.
Five scientists were chosen for the expedition, selected to represent their individual fields of study and their respective nations. British zoologist Martin Holdgate was joined by botanist
Eric Godley
(1919-2010), marine biologist George Knox (1919-2008) and geologist William Watters (1926-2014) from New Zealand, as well as entomologist
Guillermo Kuschel
(1918-2017) from Chile.
George Knox fording a river on horseback, 1958 (
MS/955/6/37
)
The expedition photos begin in Santiago in September 1958 where the party assembled and made contact with the British Council and the Chilean Air Force. Undeterred by the delayed passage of their supplies through customs, the group made a short excursion to the Andes while they waited, exploring the mountains on horseback. Once their packages were released, they travelled down to Puerto Montt by train and then flew to the first research site, Chepu on the west coast of
Chiloé Island
.
As well as reassessing sites visited by Darwin, the Southern Chile expedition also aimed to investigate species common to New Zealand, Australia and South America. In the 1950s, geological concepts such as plate tectonics were still new areas of research, and there was an active debate about the past configuration of the world’s continents. Expeditions such as this one, which showed how similar flora and fauna occur across the Southern Temperate Zone, helped to inform our modern knowledge about the history of the Earth.
Eric Godley at the coast near Chepu, 1958 (
MS/955/6/55
)
Following an exploration of the shoreline of Chepu, the party ventured further inland to research the nearby rainforests. They were making good progress with their sample collecting by this point, and already had a jar full of anaesthetised sea cucumbers and a large bowl of frogs, which they kept fed on flies.
After five weeks, the group left Chepu and moved on to their next site, the San Pedro Mountain Range at the highest point of Chiloé Island. Here they set up a base in an abandoned sheep farm and spent two weeks identifying species native to the highland forests and grasslands. Before descending to Castro, the capital of Chiloé Province, Kuschel ventured out to hunt a small deer and the party held an asado, a traditional Chilean barbecue.
From Castro the expedition party travelled south by ship to their next research site, Puerto Edén on the east coast of
Wellington Island
. Known for its extraordinarily wet and humid climate, this destination also brought the scientists into contact with a small population of indigenous
Kawésqar
people. Based in Puerto Edén for four weeks, the party used their expedition boat to explore the islands on either side of the English Narrows.
The houses and jetty at Puerto Edén, 1958 (
MS/955/6/175
)
In addition to recording the local landscapes and wildlife, the party also documented the daily life of the Kawésqar residents of Puerto Edén. These photographs provide a fascinating insight into a group of people with cultures and customs distinct from the majority of South America, including their 15ft boats, made from the trunks of southern beech trees, and their housebuilding and local crafts.
When the Chilean ship
Micalvi
passed through the settlement, the expedition party came aboard and began their voyage down to
Punta Arenas
, celebrating Christmas with the ship’s crew on Guarello Island. Arriving in Punta Arenas, they were dismayed to hear that their Christmas cards sent from home, as well as a crate of champagne and other delicacies, had been forwarded on to Puerto Edén for them, only to arrive after they had left.
Avenida Independencia in Punta Arenas, 1958 (
MS/955/6/229
)

data.title: Usenix ATC Announcement
data.author: eatbitseveryday
data.article_summary:
USENIX将于2025年庆祝成立50周年，并宣布其历史最悠久的年度技术会议（USENIX ATC）将在2025年7月后结束。自1975年成立以来，USENIX一直是高级计算系统社区创新者的重要聚集地。其年度会议在1995年合并为单一的年度技术会议（ATC），并持续了30年。然而，随着更多专注特定主题的USENIX会议加入日程，ATC的参会人数逐渐减少，无法维持必要的研究者和从业者群体。因此，USENIX董事会决定结束ATC。

ATC曾见证了许多行业“首次”，如1979年ONYX UNIX硬件、1983年Sendmail、1985年NFS等重要发布。然而，随着社区和技术的演变，其他会议如USENIX Security和FAST等逐渐吸引了更多关注。尽管ATC的结束是一个艰难的决定，但USENIX认识到变革的必然性，并感谢ATC对协会及社区的重大贡献。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：USENIX ATC（Annual Technical Conference）的现状及其在学术和工业界中的地位变化

不同观点：
• [mjb] 认为，随着OSDI变为年度会议，NSDI接受更多广泛的系统研究，ATC陷入了一个困难的定位。然而，ATC仍然为一些“更具黑客性质”的系统工作、工业系统的论文以及不太量化的研究提供了有价值的平台。他希望OSDI以及SOSP和Eurosys等会议能接受更多类似的工作。他也提到自己曾在ATC获奖，并得到积极反馈，但该论文曾被另一个会议拒之门外。

• [aoki] 指出，尽管仍有大量研究论文提交至ATC，但社区已经演变，更多人选择参加其他会议。他提到ATC的参会人数从2000年的1,698人下降到2024年的165人，并认为ATC变成了一个“只写不读”的会议。

• [zinekeller] 关注ATC的资金问题，并提到2025年ATC的黄金赞助商是国家科学基金会。他讨论了近期白宫事件的影响，并质疑这是否是一个长期存在的问题。

• [throw0101c] 指出，尽管ATC不再如从前，USENIX仍有其他会议。他提供了一些相关链接。

• [jamesblonde] 认为ATC多年来是一个伟大的会议，但其参会人数下降是因为缺乏想象力。他建议可以像其他顶级系统会议一样，将会议地点移到美国和湾区之外。

• [ferfumarma] 简单表示，这篇文章记录了一个令人遗憾的里程碑。

补充讨论：
• ATC的定位和价值受到其他会议变化的影响，如OSDI和NSDI。
• 有评论提到ATC参会人数下降的现象，并对其未来表示担忧。
• 有人质疑ATC的资金问题及其对会议的影响，并讨论了可能的外部因素。
• 有建议提出可以通过改变会议地点来提升ATC的吸引力和参与度。

争议焦点：ATC的当前价值和未来发展方向，包括其在学术和工业界的定位问题。

USENIX ATC Announcement

May 6, 2025 - 4:49 pm by jessicakim
USENIX celebrates its 50th anniversary in 2025. We celebrate decades of innovations, experiments, and gatherings of the advanced computing system community. And in the spirit of our ever-evolving community, field, and industry, we announce the bittersweet conclusion of our longest-running event, the USENIX Annual Technical Conference in July 2025, following USENIX ATC '25.
Since USENIX's inception in 1975, it has been a key gathering place for innovators in the advanced computing systems community. The early days of meetings evolved into the two annual conferences, the USENIX Summer and Winter Conferences, which in 1995 merged into the single Annual Technical Conference that has continued to evolve and serve thousands of our constituents for 30 years.
For the past two decades, as more USENIX conferences have joined the USENIX calendar by focusing on specific topics that grew out of ATC itself, attendance at ATC has steadily decreased to the point where there is no longer a critical mass of researchers and practitioners joining us. Thus, after many years of experiments to adapt this conference to the ever-changing tech landscape and community, the USENIX Board of Directors has made the difficult decision to sunset USENIX ATC.
USENIX ATC in its many iterations has been the home of an incredible list of "firsts" in our industry:
In 1979, ONYX, the first attempt at genuine UNIX hardware, was announced.
In 1982, DEC unveiled the creation of its UNIX product.
In 1983, Eric Allman presented the first paper on Sendmail, "Mail Systems and Addressing in 4.2BSD."
In 1985, Sun Microsystems presented the first paper on NFS, "Design and Implementation of the Sun Network Filesystem."
In 1988, the first light on Kerberos and the X Window system was presented.
In 1989, Tom Christiansen made his first Perl presentation as an Invited Talk.
In 1990, John Ousterhout presented Tcl.
In 1995, the first talk on Oak (later JAVA) was given as a Work-in-Progress report.
In 1998, Miguel de Icaza presented "The GNOME Desktop Environment."
These examples represent just a few of the many contributions presented at USENIX ATC over the years, with hundreds of papers that account for thousands of citations of work that the community has presented, discussed, learned from, and built upon as the community evolved.
Part of that evolution involved the continued development of subcommunities, as has been the case with USENIX Security, which began as a workshop in 1988 and has since grown to an annual symposium and the largest of our events in terms of both papers published and number of attendees annually, with 417 papers and 1,015 attendees at USENIX Security '24. The LISA (Large Installation System Administration) Conference, which also started as a workshop in 1987, grew in a similar fashion to its peak of over 1,000 attendees, but like USENIX ATC declined as its community changed until its own sunset in 2021.
Papers on file and storage systems that would have previously been presented at USENIX ATC in the early 2000s began to find homes at FAST when it was founded in 2002. Networked systems papers started flowing to NSDI in 2003. As the biennial OSDI continued to grow alongside ACM's SOSP, OSDI became annual in 2021 and SOSP followed suit, providing the community with additional venues. While landmark moments in our community have continued at USENIX ATC, many others have also occurred at these other USENIX conferences, as showcased in the
USENIX Test of Time Awards
and the
ACM SIGOPS Hall of Fame Awards
, which celebrate influential works presented at both SOSP and OSDI. Although numerous papers continue to be submitted to USENIX ATC with significant research being reviewed, accepted, and presented, the community has evolved, and now attends conferences other than USENIX ATC. From 1,698 attendees in San Diego in 2000, ATC attendance dwindled to 165 attendees in Santa Clara in 2024—even as we had over 4,000 people attend all USENIX conferences in 2024.
USENIX recognizes the pivotal role that USENIX ATC has played in the shaping of the Association itself as well as the lives and careers of its many attendees and members. USENIX将于2025年庆祝成立50周年，并宣布其历史最悠久的年度技术会议（USENIX ATC）将在2025年7月后结束。自1975年成立以来，USENIX一直是高级计算系统社区创新者的重要聚集地。其年度会议在1995年合并为单一的年度技术会议（ATC），并持续了30年。然而，随着更多专注特定主题的USENIX会议加入日程，ATC的参会人数逐渐减少，无法维持必要的研究者和从业者群体。因此，USENIX董事会决定结束ATC。

ATC曾见证了许多行业“首次”，如1979年ONYX UNIX硬件、1983年Sendmail、1985年NFS等重要发布。然而，随着社区和技术的演变，其他会议如USENIX Security和FAST等逐渐吸引了更多关注。尽管ATC的结束是一个艰难的决定，但USENIX认识到变革的必然性，并感谢ATC对协会及社区的重大贡献。

data.article_summary:
这篇文章主要讨论了C++中的隐式转换序列（implicit conversion sequence），特别是关于限定符转换（qualification conversion）的细节。文章首先引入了标准转换序列的概念，包括左值到右值、数组到指针、函数到指针的转换，以及积分、浮点、布尔、指针和成员指针转换等。然后，文章重点讲解了限定符转换，特别是`const`和`volatile`在类型中的作用。

作者详细分析了如何将复杂类型用`const`和`volatile`的嵌套形式表示，并提出了通过去除顶层限定符来简化类型转换的判断方法。文章最后将类型转换问题归结为一个关于限定符的n元组，以帮助理解类型之间的转换关系。总体而言，文章旨在帮助读者更好地理解C++中的类型转换机制，尤其是涉及限定符的部分。

data.title: eBPF Mystery: When is IPv4 not IPv4? When it's pretending to be IPv6
data.author: tanelpoder
data.article_summary:
这篇文章描述了一次使用eBPF程序透明地重定向DNS请求的冒险经历，最初目标是重定向单个程序（或Docker容器）在端口53上的DNS请求。作者通过在cgroup上使用BPF_CGROUP_INET4_CONNECT来检查和重定向syscall.connect发生的流量。起初，一切顺利，但当用户尝试使用dotnet CLI时，程序出现了挂起问题，并产生了大量PACKET_IPV6_TYPE阻塞消息。

尽管网络流量显示为IPv4，但eBPF程序却检测到IPv6请求。通过深入研究，作者发现.NET 5之后的DualMode sockets特性允许通过IPv6套接字处理IPv4流量，这导致eBPF程序的行为异常。具体原因是IPv4-mapped IPv6地址的使用，这种地址将IPv4地址编码在IPv6地址中。

最终，通过禁用DualMode sockets特性，问题得以解决，eBPF程序正常工作。这次经历揭示了网络协议底层的一些复杂交互，特别是IPv4和IPv6的兼容性机制。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：IPv4与IPv6地址的兼容性处理及其在不同操作系统和网络配置中的实现方式

不同观点：
• [zzq1015] 提出在Linux系统中，通过调整内核设置（`sysctl -w net.ipv6.bindv6only=1`）可以让IPv6不包含IPv4映射地址，从而实现更纯粹的IPv6使用。
• [brewmarche] 指出IPv4兼容地址和IPv4映射地址是不同的概念，前者（::/96）已不再使用，后者（::ffff:0:0/96）则常用于同时绑定IPv4和IPv6的套接字。此外，还提到了其他将IPv4嵌入IPv6的方式，如NAT64和6to4。
• [IcePic] 认为像OpenBSD这样不允许在IPv6套接字上处理IPv4的操作系统可能有其道理。虽然让程序员只需监听一个套接字很方便，但这会导致后续处理中的复杂性，特别是在日志记录等方面。因此，强制应用程序对两种协议进行分离处理可能是更正确的选择。
• [degamad] 认为IPv6套接字假装成IPv4来进行路由是一种反向操作，即IPv6套接字用于处理IPv4端点的路由。
• [Almondsetat] 表示嵌入IPv4地址到IPv6字段中是Linux支持的一种正式定义的单播IPv6地址类型，并指出这是官方定义的特性，甚至在Wikipedia上也有相关描述。

补充讨论：
• [smitty1e] 分享了一个Python脚本中的类似情况，通过调用一个C程序来处理字符编码，而实际上Python的`open()`函数本身就支持编码参数，这表明有时候复杂的解决方案可能是因为不了解工具的全部功能。
• [dilfish] 提到在使用Go的`net.ListenTCP`时，通过`lsof`查看网络类型会显示为IPv6，但它也能处理IPv4请求。
• [imoverclocked] 进一步介绍了6to4和6over4的区别，指出通过嵌入全球唯一的IPv4地址可以创建自动隧道的IPv6网络。
• [gitroom] 则对所有这些让网络通信变得可能的技巧表示赞赏，并质疑这些技巧是因为习惯还是为了走捷径而存在。

争议焦点：
• IPv4映射地址在IPv6套接字中的使用是否合理，是否应该强制应用程序对两种协议进行分离处理，以避免潜在的复杂性和混淆。
• 对IPv4和IPv6地址嵌入技术的不同理解，特别是对IPv4兼容地址和IPv4映射地址的区分。

这篇文章描述了一次使用eBPF程序透明地重定向DNS请求的冒险经历，最初目标是重定向单个程序（或Docker容器）在端口53上的DNS请求。作者通过在cgroup上使用BPF_CGROUP_INET4_CONNECT来检查和重定向syscall.connect发生的流量。起初，一切顺利，但当用户尝试使用dotnet CLI时，程序出现了挂起问题，并产生了大量PACKET_IPV6_TYPE阻塞消息。

尽管网络流量显示为IPv4，但eBPF程序却检测到IPv6请求。通过深入研究，作者发现.NET 5之后的DualMode sockets特性允许通过IPv6套接字处理IPv4流量，这导致eBPF程序的行为异常。具体原因是IPv4-mapped IPv6地址的使用，这种地址将IPv4地址编码在IPv6地址中。

最终，通过禁用DualMode sockets特性，问题得以解决，eBPF程序正常工作。这次经历揭示了网络协议底层的一些复杂交互，特别是IPv4和IPv6的兼容性机制。
43933683.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：IPv4与IPv6地址的兼容性处理及其在不同操作系统和网络配置中的实现方式

不同观点：
• [zzq1015] 提出在Linux系统中，通过调整内核设置（`sysctl -w net.ipv6.bindv6only=1`）可以让IPv6不包含IPv4映射地址，从而实现更纯粹的IPv6使用。
• [brewmarche] 指出IPv4兼容地址和IPv4映射地址是不同的概念，前者（::/96）已不再使用，后者（::ffff:0:0/96）则常用于同时绑定IPv4和IPv6的套接字。此外，还提到了其他将IPv4嵌入IPv6的方式，如NAT64和6to4。
• [IcePic] 认为像OpenBSD这样不允许在IPv6套接字上处理IPv4的操作系统可能有其道理。虽然让程序员只需监听一个套接字很方便，但这会导致后续处理中的复杂性，特别是在日志记录等方面。因此，强制应用程序对两种协议进行分离处理可能是更正确的选择。
• [degamad] 认为IPv6套接字假装成IPv4来进行路由是一种反向操作，即IPv6套接字用于处理IPv4端点的路由。
• [Almondsetat] 表示嵌入IPv4地址到IPv6字段中是Linux支持的一种正式定义的单播IPv6地址类型，并指出这是官方定义的特性，甚至在Wikipedia上也有相关描述。

补充讨论：
• [smitty1e] 分享了一个Python脚本中的类似情况，通过调用一个C程序来处理字符编码，而实际上Python的`open()`函数本身就支持编码参数，这表明有时候复杂的解决方案可能是因为不了解工具的全部功能。
• [dilfish] 提到在使用Go的`net.ListenTCP`时，通过`lsof`查看网络类型会显示为IPv6，但它也能处理IPv4请求。
• [imoverclocked] 进一步介绍了6to4和6over4的区别，指出通过嵌入全球唯一的IPv4地址可以创建自动隧道的IPv6网络。
• [gitroom] 则对所有这些让网络通信变得可能的技巧表示赞赏，并质疑这些技巧是因为习惯还是为了走捷径而存在。

争议焦点：
• IPv4映射地址在IPv6套接字中的使用是否合理，是否应该强制应用程序对两种协议进行分离处理，以避免潜在的复杂性和混淆。
• 对IPv4和IPv6地址嵌入技术的不同理解，特别是对IPv4兼容地址和IPv4映射地址的区分。

• Midasz认为该软件是自托管世界的支柱之一，并与其他自托管服务进行比较。
• Kyriakos推荐PinePods用于播客管理，指出其跨平台支持和功能上的不足。
• InsideOutSanta寻找无DRM音频书籍的来源，以替代Audible。
• Heisenzombie质疑在自托管音频书籍服务器上复制播客的用例。
• Apitman询问关于API开发的经验。

• 用户对自托管解决方案的元数据管理和离线功能有较高需求，并提出了自动化和AI工具的潜在解决方案。

• 对API开发的讨论可能吸引开发者社区的兴趣，并推动应用程序功能的扩展和改进。

data.title: Throwaway Code: Don't recycle, throw it away (2017)
data.author: sails
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了在编程项目中遇到问题时，使用"一次性代码"（Throwaway Code）练习的重要性。作者在开发一个React侧边项目时，因频繁调试React问题而进展缓慢，导致时间分配失衡。为解决此问题，作者阅读了《Pure React》一书，并根据书中建议，针对每个练习创建一次性代码，而不是花费时间在设置GitHub仓库等仪式性工作上。通过这种方法，作者快速创建了一个原型，并向朋友展示了成果。文章最后建议，遇到编码问题时，应多次使用一次性代码进行练习，以掌握概念。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：软件开发中原型设计与代码质量、任务规模判断以及代码保留与否的策略

不同观点：
• [klabb3] 主张对于中等规模且包含许多未知因素的任务，应先积极进行低质量的原型设计以快速学习，然后在第二轮迭代中关注质量。这种方式比直接设计并构建更有效，因为通过实践获取的新知识能简化实现过程，并避免分析瘫痪（analysis paralysis）。难点在于预先判断任务的规模。

• [RedShift1] 反对随意丢弃代码，提到自己不会丢弃80多个“新”的notepad++标签页，暗示保留代码的重要性。

• [athrowaway3z] 建议创建一个存档目录来保存旧代码，而不是直接丢弃，这样可以通过定期检索来回顾和反思过去的错误，同时保留有用的代码。

• [1dom] 支持 [klabb3] 的观点，认为原型设计的价值在于快速学习和推进，而非提倡丢弃代码。同时指出，数字世界中的存储和操作几乎没有成本，因此保留数字产物通常比物理世界更有益。

• [gherkinnn] 强调代码本身不是唯一的宝贵产物，开发过程中获得的知识更为重要。

• [gitroom] 提到自己保存了大量混乱的文件，质疑保留旧代码是否会拖慢开发进度或者实际上有助于长期学习。

• [mehulashah] 欣赏从无到有构建系统的美丽，认为如果系统规模足够大，不可能频繁地重新开始，暗示大规模系统需要更谨慎的规划和保留现有代码。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于是否应该保留原型代码，一些人认为保留代码有价值，而另一些人则主张在获取新知识后可以丢弃代码以轻装上阵。
• 讨论中也涉及了任务规模判断的困难，以及不同规模任务对开发策略的影响。
• 知识获取和代码存储的相对价值是另一个值得注意的讨论点，部分人认为知识比代码本身更重要。

43905153.article_content:
2017-09-05
Throwaway Code: Don't recycle, throw it away!
blogentry, programming, slightedge, todayilearned
OK, you are working on a side programming project, and it's not progressing.
Probably you aren't the only one. I've been working on a side project using React and ran into a problem.
This is just one of the many ways of that will help you to advance your project.
TLDL; Exercise often with "Throwaway" code.
Context
I've watched many online courses (Udemy/PluralSight) and read many blog article on React. I had a fun idea for a side project and decided to get started.
Problem Faced
I muddled through and made progresses. But the project stalled because I was constantly having problems with simple React errors. Eventually I was spending more time on debugging React issues than on the project itself.
There is an idiom in Korean,
The belly button is bigger than the belly (배보다 배꼽이 더크다).
It basically means that your priority has been reversed. In my case, I was spending more time on fixing React issues than making a project progress.
What I Did
I decided to focus purely on React and found a book called
Pure React
by Dave Ceddia.
Dave instructed to create
Throwaway codes
for each exercises in the book. Until learning into this concept, I've been doing useless ceremony of setting up a
GitHub repos
with "Demo." prefix, which hindered me to do quick and dirty prototyping.
I created a myriad of throwaway codes for each exercise.
Result
I showed one my exercises (GitHub clone) with fake data to one of my friends (Please overlook CSS issues...)
He then asked me if I can use a real live news data. I thought, "Challenge Accepted".
After creating so many throwaway codes, I was able to quickly create a prototype in about 30 minutes and shared it with
LocalTunnel
. (Please pardon my CSS skills, again...)
The friend? Blown away.
Takeaway
When having a coding problem, practice as many time as possible with throwaway codes.
You just learn the concept and throw it away.

data.title: Product Purgatory: When they love it but still don't buy
data.author: doppp
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了“产品炼狱”（Product Purgatory）现象，即潜在客户虽然喜欢产品但不购买的情况。创始人往往渴望得到认可，误将客户的客气话当作产品验证。即使客户真心喜欢产品，仍可能因实施过程中的风险、时间和成本等问题而不购买。文章引入“魔法棒测试”：即使产品免费并完全实施，客户也可能拒绝，因为新产品带来的摩擦和潜在问题（如安全和兼容性）可能超过其价值。对新公司而言，缺乏品牌和记录增加了客户的顾虑，即使产品解决实际问题，若价值未显著超过使用成本和风险，客户仍不会购买。改变困难且时间有限，客户更关注能带来重大影响的产品。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：产品为何会陷入“ purgatory ”（指产品虽被用户喜欢但未被实际购买的情况）

不同观点：
• **rdtsc 的观点**：产品陷入“purgatory”的一个原因是客户已经在使用类似产品。市场调研时，虽然客户表示有需求、喜欢产品并愿意付费，但调研者往往忘记询问客户是否已经在使用类似产品。如果客户已经在使用其他类似产品，新产品可能难以获得市场份额。这个遗漏的问题可能导致产品开发后遭遇销售失败。

• **steveBK123 的观点**：有些产品虽然受到好评，但并没有带来实际销售。例如，Sigma的相机镜头虽然设计精良、评价积极，但往往是“已经有其他相机的人”才会购买。这表明有些产品设计独特但销售不佳，可能是因为它们没有真正简化用户的生活，反而增加了复杂性。因此，在软件行业也应考虑产品是否真正简化了用户的工作流程或取代了现有工具，而不是仅仅增加了复杂性。

• **FinnLobsien 的观点**：产品是否被购买与产品的购买方式密切相关。一些产品是通过发现和尝试而被用户接受的，但这些产品常常陷入“purgatory”。相反，基础设施类的产品（如计费和计量工具）不太可能通过偶然发现而被购买，通常需要经过正式的采购流程和多方比较。这类产品的购买决策更具目的性，但它们缺乏病毒式传播的潜力。

补充讨论：
• 产品陷入“purgatory”的原因包括客户已经在使用类似产品、产品增加了用户复杂性以及产品的购买决策流程较为正式和慎重。
• 不同类型的产品（如消费类产品与基础设施类产品）面临的购买决策过程不同，消费类产品更容易通过新奇性吸引用户，但基础设施类产品则更依赖于正式的采购流程和比较。
• 争议的焦点在于如何在市场调研阶段全面了解客户的真实需求和现有使用情况，以避免开发出虽受欢迎但不被购买的产品。

Product Purgatory: When they love it but still donât buy
by Jason Cohen on May 4, 2025
source
Most people say nice things when you pitch your product. âOh, that looks really great! I like it, but weâre not buying right now. Maybe call back later in the year?â Itâs hard to tell you that your baby is ugly.
This creates a trap for new founders who are (rightly!) infatuated with their ideas. They yearn so desperately for validationânominally product validation but actually personal validationâthat they interpret these kindly social white lies as confirmation.
But sometimes the potential customer
really does
love it. They
really do
wish they could buy it. And yet, theyâre still not buying, or at least ânot yet.â You have the distinct feeling they werenât just being niceâthey were genuine. And yet, the purchase never happens.
This is Product Purgatory.
Not even with a magic wand
Itâs amazing how many products fail an even simpler test of desirability and viability. I call it the Magic Wand Test, and it works like this:
I have a magic wand, and when I wave it, our product will be fully implemented in your company. Everyone is trained. Other tools are integrated. Processes are changed. Security requirements are satisfied. And best of all, it is
completely free
!
So! Do you want me to wave this magic wand?
Shockingly, the answer is often:
âNo.â
How could they say âNo!?â If the product delivers any value whatsoever, you might as well take it, right? No, because all products not only create friction in implementation, but risk and time and money, often on-going, and the Magic Wand Test proves it. The value of the product must
significantly exceed
this activation energy.
A great example of this was an Austin-based startup twenty years ago. There were a spate of news stories about employees leaking secret corporate documents via email.
1
So this startup created a solution: All corporate email would flow through the startupâs servers, where the content is scanned for sensitive material. Questionable things could be returned to the sender or otherwise flagged.
2
1
This risk continues to the present day. In 2017 a Boeing employee
accidentally emailed his spouse
a spreadsheet with personal information of 36,000 coworkers. Boeing offering two years of free credit monitoring to affected employees at an estimated cost of $7,000,000.
2
In another fascinating example of how companies solve this problem on their own, in 2008 Tesla faced a situation where confidential company information was being leaked to the press. Tesla
implemented a clever method
to identify the leaker: Send a unique email to each employee, differing only in things like white space and punctuation, so that when the press reprinted that information using copy/paste, those details would identify the source.
Despite the very real problem they solved, they couldnât get anyone to buy it. The reason wasnât that people didnât care about leaks; the news stories were real. The reason was that, even if you could have it for free, there is just too much risk in putting a brand new startup in the middle of all your email. Thereâs the obvious security issue of a probably-hackable startup, and someone elseâs employees potentially having access to all your email. Also bugs. If this new company has bugsâand doesnât all new software have bugs?âthat would compromise email, which is catastrophic. So although there was some value, and a real problem, the value did not significantly exceed the penalty of using the product.
In the real world the Magic Wand doesnât exist; even if the price is fair, there are real costs and disruption of implementation and training and integration, and people simply getting used to a new user interface and processes and therefore being unproductive for a while. Product inventors revel in all the value they generate, but donât see the penalties that they incur. The customers, however, see.
Furthermore, itâs not good enough for value to merely exceed penalty; the value must be
far larger
than the penalty. If the value is only slightly larger, itâs not worth engaging, not worth the money, not worth the risk.
Change is difficult
and
time is limited
; customers cannot spend their time on things that have only minor impact.
This challenge looms even larger for new companies, because you have neither brand nor track record. Thatâs even more risk, including that youâre out of business in two years or that your product canât handle real-world use-cases. Even for free, many types of customer are not willing to take those risks. I donât want to use âthe newest code libraryâ for anything except fun throw-away projects, because I donât want to rip and replace in a few years, and I want thousands of bugs to have already been found and eradicated, and I want to be able to hire people who already have experience with the library.

data.author: raybb
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了政府补贴Citi Bike的利弊。随着Citi Bike使用量创下新高，其费用也在快速上涨，一年内涨幅接近50%。布鲁克林议员Ossé和Restler提出立法，建议将会员费上限设为与地铁票价相同（2.90美元），以鼓励更多人使用自行车而非开车。文章分析了这一提案的可行性，指出美国许多公共交通机构依赖税收等外部收入，而Citi Bike目前没有此类补贴。文章还提到，一些北美城市已用公共资金支持 bikeshare 网络。若实施新的收费上限，估计每年需约2525万美元的补贴，以弥补收入损失。文章最后提出，是否补贴需根据具体数据和政策决定。

Richard Levine / Alamy Stock Photo
If Free Buses Aren’t Wise, What About Cheaper Citi Bikes?
Austin Celestin
April 23, 2025
Weighing the pros and cons of government subsidizing bike shares
Weighing the pros and cons of government subsidizing bike shares
It’s easy to forget that there was a time when Citi Bike wasn’t a ubiquitous presence on our streets. Last year, the network of Lyft-operated, blue-and-grey two-wheelers hit new heights, as riders
set three daily
and
two monthly
ridership records on the way to reaching
250 million all-time rides
. Citi Bike has become a mainstay on our streets, and the soaring ridership isn’t showing any signs of slowing down.
The only thing rising faster than Citi Bike’s ridership numbers is its fees. On New Year’s Day in 2024, the e-bike fare was $0.17 per minute for members and $0.26 per minute for non-members. Three days later,
the rate rose to $0.20 for members and $0.30 for non-members
. Six months later,
the fare jumped again to $0.24 for members and $0.36 for non-members
. And this past January,
the fee rose one last time to $0.25 for members and $0.38 for non-members
, totaling at a nearly 50% price hike in just over a year. It’s a trend that advocates and planners have sought to reverse as part of a broader push to
publicly fund Citi Bike
. Those efforts have failed to gain traction in the City Council.
That changed last fall, when Brooklyn Councilmembers Chi Ossé and Lincoln Restler introduced
legislation
to cap Citi Bike fares for members at the cost of a subway fare: $2.90. The fare cap would apply to all rides on e-bikes under an hour (or two hours for conventional, non-pedal-assist bikes). Ossé and Restler hope the fare cap incentivizes drivers to switch from driving to using Citi Bike.
This marks the most concrete push to reduce the cost of Citi Bike with the help of public subsidies. The efforts mirror the
free bus initiative
that Queens Assemblyman and mayoral candidate Zohran Mamdani has advocated for. In October,
I analyzed Mamdani’s plan
(and fare-free transit writ large) and recommended against implementing it. With Citi Bike fare cuts, similar dynamics and viability questions are at play. However, some variables argue in favor of bringing down the price of bikeshare.
How we got here
What Ossé and Restler are proposing for Citi Bike is standard practice for American public transit agencies; fares typically comprise a fraction of the revenue agencies receive. The MTA, for example,
only gets around a quarter of its revenue from fares
— the rest comes from taxes, tolls and federal COVID aid. Los Angeles’ ratio is
even lower, at 5%
. These lower ratios are due to post-pandemic ridership drops; in 2019,
the MTA’s farebox recovery ratio was 53%
, one of eight transit agencies nationwide with recovery ratios over 50%. Still, transit agencies routinely get a lot of outside revenue support beyond their fares, whereas Citi Bike currently gets nothing. The full implementation of Intro 1039 would bring the bikeshare’s recovery ratio down to 60%, exceeding all but three American transit agencies’ pre-pandemic recovery ratios. This request would seem entirely reasonable if Citi Bike were a subway system.
But one doesn’t have to point to public transit subsidies as justification for a bikeshare subsidy;
several North American cities already dedicate public subsidies to help fund their bikeshare networks
, like Mexico City, Montreal, San Francisco, Washington D.C. and Boston. Typically, these cities used the money to fund operations rather than fare cuts. (Boston did allocate $550,000 for subsidized passes during MBTA closures in 2022). But there is plenty of precedent for using public funds to help pay for bikeshares. Nothing is preventing the City Council from dedicating subsidies to replacing fares.
To establish how much public money is needed, we must establish how much revenue we need to replace, which requires creating a new fare structure with the cap. For simplicity’s sake, I will round up to $3. Currently, Citi Bike caps rides across boroughs at the equivalent of a 20-minute fare ($5 plus tax), so we can use that interborough limit as a model for our cap. Setting the price at $3 for a 20-minute-or-longer ride translates to a $0.15 per minute fare for the first 20 minutes and then free fare beyond that. Therefore, a subsidy would have to replace 40% of the revenue for the first 20 minutes of a ride and the entire fare beyond that.
In 2024,
Citi Bike raked in about $215 million in total revenue, $80 million of which came from e-bikes
. In 2022,
NYU Wagner’s Rudin Center
estimated that members accounted for 79% of Citi Bike rides. That puts the approximate subsidy requirement at about $25.25 million annually. That estimate does not consider the 20% of rides that exceed 20 minutes, which must be entirely replaced from the 21st minute. However, there is also a higher e-bike fee that non-members must pay, decreasing members’ overall contribution and balancing out th

主要讨论点：加州社区大学财务援助欺诈问题及其背后的系统性漏洞

• **autoexec** 认为问题的核心不在于课堂上的假学生，而在于发放财务援助前没有严格验证身份。建议通过仅发放校内可使用的信用额度来防止欺诈，而非直接发放现金。
• **miki123211** 分享了之前涉及CCSF的类似欺诈案例，指出在2018-19年期间，有人通过伪造的CCSF电子邮件账户进行欺诈，且这些账户在Google Drive等服务上出售。认为CCSF在身份验证上存在漏洞。
• **SayItAintSo2** 强调学校和教职工通过虚假的注册学生获取利益，而纳税人则为此买单。指出社区大学在学生出勤和身份验证上监管不力，导致欺诈行为长期存在。
• **jccalhoun** 表示这一问题不仅限于加州，中西部的社区大学也存在类似问题。指出在线课程中存在大量假学生，且这些学生起初会提交作业，增加了教师的工作负担。
• **rdtsc** 质疑媒体报道的表面性，认为报道没有深入解释问题的根源。指出CCSF在身份验证上存在明显的漏洞，且验证过程是可选的，使得欺诈行为容易发生。
• **paxys** 认为0.21%的欺诈率在可接受范围内，因为完全消除欺诈将需要过多的资源，并可能导致合格的申请被错误拒绝。
• **toast0** 质疑将所有未出勤学生视为欺诈的定义，指出有些学生可能只是临时注册而没有实际意图入学。同时，提出加州社区大学的低入学门槛可能导致大量无意入学的注册。
• **stretchwithme** 认为加州的多个项目设计上存在系统性漏洞，导致欺诈行为频繁发生，并暗示政府在管理上缺乏常识。
• **rahimnathwani** 解释了加州社区大学的资金分配公式，指出假学生可以增加学校的资金收入，从而减少学校领导排除假学生的动机。
• **qoez** 针对文章中提到的“机器人背后有人类操作”的观点，强调所有机器人行为背后必然有人类操作。
• **nandomrumber** 对“财务援助被欺诈性发放”的措辞提出质疑，认为更准确的表述应为“欺诈性索取”。
• **phoenixreader** 惊讶于在美国大学昂贵的背景下，有人可以通过虚假注册获取财务援助。
• **kylehotchkiss** 用讽刺的语气指出，被浪费的资金本可以用于建设更有益的公共设施，如自行车道。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到身份验证系统的漏洞，尤其是CCSF的可选身份验证过程，这使得欺诈行为容易发生。
• 有人质疑媒体报道的深度，认为报道没有充分解释问题的复杂性和系统性漏洞。
• 讨论中涉及了加州社区大学的低入学门槛和资金分配机制，这可能激励学校对假学生问题视而不见。
• 争议的焦点在于如何定义和处理欺诈行为，尤其是如何平衡严格的身份验证和确保合格申请人的权益。

data.title: Doge software engineer's computer infected by info-stealing malware
data.author: lysp
data.article_summary: 一名在网络安全和基础设施安全局（CISA）及政府效率部门（DOGE）工作的软件工程师凯尔·舒特（Kyle Schutt）的登录信息多次出现在信息窃取恶意软件的公开泄露中，表明他的设备近年来曾被黑客入侵。自2023年以来，舒特的用户名和密码至少四次被恶意软件日志公开，涉及多起数据泄露事件，包括Adobe、LinkedIn和Gravatar等。尽管单次泄露不一定表明个人使用了弱密码，但频繁出现表明其凭证曾多次公开暴露。若他在CISA和DOGE工作中使用了相同或相似凭证，攻击者可能已获取敏感信息。相关部门未对此事立即回应，而批评者指出DOGE在安全操作上存在诸多问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于某人的设备被黑客攻击及其对安全的影响的讨论

不同观点：
• 一种观点认为，糟糕的操作安全性（0pSec）可能是故意的，有人故意泄露秘密，以此作为背叛行为的借口。这种观点暗示某些人（如评论中提到的俄罗斯）可能从中获利，且以无能作为合理的否认借口。  
   （代表评论：[amelius]）

• 另一种观点质疑是否有足够的证据支持这种阴谋论，指出自己的电子邮件也曾出现在数据泄露中，而这并不能直接证明系统中存在键盘记录器。这种观点认为批评某些组织的重大失误是重要的，但这种文章降低了新闻 journalism 的可信度。  
   （代表评论：[whacko_quacko]）

• 有人批评这种推测性文章和点击诱饵式的标题，认为读者不应一再被这种垃圾信息所迷惑。  
   （代表评论：[dev_l1x_be]）

• 有评论指出，问题不仅在于密码泄露，而是涉及“窃取恶意软件”，这些恶意软件通过木马程序、钓鱼或软件漏洞感染设备，并泄露用户名和密码。  
   （代表评论：[palata]）

• 另一种观点关注安全措施的缺失，质疑为什么当事人不使用机构提供的电脑，并指出在安全系统中不应依赖简单密码，而应使用如Active Directory角色和证书等更高级的安全措施。  
   （代表评论：[ninalanyon]）

• 有人认为，这种严重无视安全、道德、法律和宪法的行为应受到严厉惩罚，甚至终身监禁。  
   （代表评论：[sys_64738]）

• 有人从个人角度出发，认为这种事件提醒自己检查密码和安全习惯，强调需要谨慎。  
   （代表评论：[gitroom]）

• 有人提出问题，是否存在某种权威机构可以剥夺那些操作安全性差的人的特权数据访问权限，例如撤销安全许可。  
   （代表评论：[ndsipa_pomu]）

• 一种怀疑论调认为，数据泄露并不罕见，质疑是否只要账户被泄露过的人都不应在政府机构工作。  
   （代表评论：[constantcrying]）

补充讨论：
• 有人以讽刺的口吻评论，认为这种事件是在为政府节省数据泄露清理的费用。  
   （代表评论：[mystified5016]）

• 有人预测相关方会隐瞒、遗漏和否认所有事实，持续数年。  
   （代表评论：[tjpnz]）

Login credentials belonging to an employee at both the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency and the Department of Government Efficiency have appeared in multiple public leaks from info-stealer malware, a strong indication that devices belonging to him have been hacked in recent years.
Kyle Schutt is a 30-something-year-old software engineer who, according to
Dropsite News
, gained access in February to a “core financial management system” belonging to the Federal Emergency Management Agency. As an employee of DOGE, Schutt accessed FEMA’s proprietary software for managing both disaster and non-disaster funding grants. Under his role at CISA, he likely is privy to sensitive information regarding the security of civilian federal government networks and critical infrastructure throughout the US.
A steady stream of published credentials
According to journalist
Micah Lee
, user names and passwords for logging in to various accounts belonging to Schutt have been published at least four times since 2023 in logs from stealer malware. Stealer malware typically infects devices through trojanized apps, phishing, or software exploits. Besides pilfering login credentials, stealers can also log all keystrokes and capture or record screen output. The data is then sent to the attacker and, occasionally after that, can make its way into public credential dumps.
“I have no way of knowing exactly when Schutt's computer was hacked, or how many times,” Lee wrote. “I don't know nearly enough about the origins of these stealer log datasets. He might have gotten hacked years ago and the stealer log datasets were just published recently. But he also might have gotten hacked within the last few months.”
Lee went on to say that credentials belonging to a Gmail account known to belong to Schutt have appeared in 51 data breaches and five pastes tracked by breach notification service
Have I Been Pwned
. Among the breaches that supplied the credentials is one from 2013 that pilfered password data for
3 million
Adobe account holders, one in a 2016 breach that stole credentials for
164 million LinkedIn users
, a 2020 breach affecting 167 million users of Gravatar, and a breach last year of the conservative news site The Post Millennial.
As Lee notes, the presence of an individual’s credentials in such logs isn’t automatically an indication that the individual himself was compromised or used a weak password. In many cases, such data is exposed through database compromises that hit the service provider. The steady stream of published credentials for Schutt, however, is a clear indication that the credentials he has used over a decade or more have been publicly known at various points.
In the event, however, that Schutt used the same or similar credentials in systems or machines during his work at CISA and DOGE, attackers may already have been able to access sensitive information he’s privy to. And as Lee noted, the four dumps from stealer logs show that at least one of his devices was hacked at some point.
DOGE critics said Lee’s findings are consistent with other operational security gaffes by the office, such as a
website that could be edited by anyone
and unprecedented and extraordinarily broad access to government data like that stored in the
federal payroll system
.
“At this point it's difficult not to suspect their awful 0pSec is a choice, and that there are specific people (*ahem* *cough cough* the Russians *cough*) to whom they're leaking secrets, with incompetence being merely plausible deniability for their true, treasonous agenda,” one critic
wrote
on Mastodon.
Representatives at CISA and the Department of Homeland Security—the agency that oversees CISA—didn’t immediately respond to an email seeking confirmation of the report.

Dan Goodin
Senior Security Editor
Dan Goodin is Senior Security Editor at Ars Technica, where he oversees coverage of malware, computer espionage, botnets, hardware hacking, encryption, and passwords. In his spare time, he enjoys gardening, cooking, and following the independent music scene. Dan is based in San Francisco. Follow him at

data.title: 6502 Illegal Opcodes in the Siemens PC 100 Assembly Manual (1980)
data.author: matt_d
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了1980年西门子PC 100编程手册中对6502处理器“非法”操作码的记录。西门子PC 100基于Rockwell AIM-65单板计算机，配备6502处理器，用于教育和开发。手册中包含了对“特殊指令”（如AAX、DCM、LAX、ISB等）的描述，这些指令并非官方规范的一部分，可能随时改变，且无法被汇编程序解码，需使用.BYT指令手动编程。西门子的描述包括了操作、标志位影响、寻址模式和操作码等细节，尽管部分指令被标记为“不稳定”或未完全正确。文章推测这些内容可能是西门子的原创研究，或者引自未公开的来源。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：德语技术术语的历史使用及其影响，以及现代处理器中未公开指令的概念

不同观点：
• weinzierl认为，当时的德国出版物倾向于使用德语术语，特别是Siemens在这方面最为激进。例如，堆栈相关的术语常围绕“地下室”（Keller）的比喻，如“einkellern”表示push，“auskellern”表示pop。这种用法可能受到Friedrich L. Bauer工作的影响。他还提到某个手册虽然简化了术语，但仍保留了一些复杂的复合词。

• toolslive补充提到，这些德语术语也曾被德国杂志《64er》广泛讨论，并提供了一个相关链接。

• eqvinox表达了一种怀旧和感伤的情绪，认为过去的德国工程代表了更多的努力和用心，暗示现代可能失去了这种精神。

• zombot引用了一段关于未公开指令（如LAX Immediate, AAX X reg $02和AAX X reg accu $02）可能未被正确处理的技术问题，并推测这可能是它们未被记录在文档中的原因。

• moring对未公开指令进行了更深入的思考，提出在现代处理器中使用可编程指令集计算机（PISC）的概念。他设想这种架构具有不变的后端（如RISC+向量），但前端有一个可编程的解码器，允许不同代码使用不同的优化编码。他认为这种方法可能对VLIW后端更有意义，而对于纯RISC架构则未必值得。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的历史性德语术语使用及其技术影响，特别是对堆栈术语的独特翻译。
• 未公开指令的技术问题及其在现代处理器架构设计中的潜在应用和挑战。
• 对过去工程实践的怀旧情绪与现代技术发展的对比。

争议焦点：
• 对德语术语使用的历史影响有不同的看法，部分人认为这是过去工程精神的体现，而现代可能不再重视。
• 关于未公开指令在现代处理器中应用的可行性和价值存在不同见解，特别是PISC概念的实际应用潜力。

The 6502’s
“illegal” opcodes
were of intense interest to home computer enthusiasts, and analyses were published in
various
magazines
. But one would have never expected a company like Siemens to document illegal opcodes in a programming manual from 1980.
The PC 100 Assembly Manual
The Siemens PC 100 is basically a Rockwell AIM-65 single-board computer in a case, featuring a 6502 processor, integrated keyboard, LED display, and thermal printer, tailored for educational and development purposes with localized documentation and modified ROMs.
Siemens’ German-language manuals  were largely based on Rockwell’s originals, but shuffled the contents. Of particular interest is the assembly manual:
Siemens Assembler-Handbuch Personal-Computer PC 100, Ausgabe 1980/1981
(124 pages, 17 MB)
It consists of:

43934279.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了1980年西门子PC 100编程手册中对6502处理器“非法”操作码的记录。西门子PC 100基于Rockwell AIM-65单板计算机，配备6502处理器，用于教育和开发。手册中包含了对“特殊指令”（如AAX、DCM、LAX、ISB等）的描述，这些指令并非官方规范的一部分，可能随时改变，且无法被汇编程序解码，需使用.BYT指令手动编程。西门子的描述包括了操作、标志位影响、寻址模式和操作码等细节，尽管部分指令被标记为“不稳定”或未完全正确。文章推测这些内容可能是西门子的原创研究，或者引自未公开的来源。

• toolslive补充提到，这些德语术语也曾被德国杂志《64er》广泛讨论，并提供了一个相关链接。

data.article_summary: ZombieVerter VCU是一款开源的电动车转换控制单元，专为控制 salvaged 电动车部件设计。它支持多种常见 salvaged 部件，如日产Leaf、三菱Outlander和丰田普锐斯的电机、电池和充电器等。该VCU具有丰富的输入/输出接口、控制逻辑以及基于网页的配置和数据记录界面，功能强大且灵活。硬件方面，配备了WiFi、CANbus接口、高侧和低侧驱动器等；软件方面，支持接触器、充电器、电机控制等多种功能。用户可以自行组装VCU板，预编程板可通过web界面进行配置和使用。ZombieVerter还支持多种BMS系统和车载CAN总线控制，适用于多种车型。

Introduction
Modern EV conversion projects often look to reuse salvaged parts from wrecked vehicles, such as the motors, batteries and chargers.
The issue is that each of these components and manufacturers, use different methods of control and communication.
Developing controllers for these devices is complex, and time consuming and often require very dedicated communication protocols. Instead of making custom boards for every part that's been decoded, why not just make a general purpose VCU (vehicle control unit) with a verity of different types of inputs and outputs?
Introducing: the "ZombieVerter" VCU
- a general purpose EV conversion VCU.
With a large array of inputs/outputs, control logic, and a web interface for configuration and data logging. The ZombieVerter is a powerful, flexible and customizable VCU well suited for EV conversions.
It's also an open source project!
The ZombieVerter supports popular salvaged EV parts such as:
Nissan Leaf components
Mitsubishi Outlander hybrid components
Toyota and Lexus hybrid components
CHAdeMO and CCS DC fast charging
and more!

data.title: Verification, the Key to AI (2001)
data.author: anjneymidha
data.article_summary: Rich Sutton的《验证，AI的关键》一文指出，AI成功的关键在于其能够自我验证是否正常工作。自我验证使得AI系统能够自主评估和修正错误，而不依赖人类干预。文章提出了“验证原则”：AI系统只能在其能够自我验证知识的范围内创建和维护知识。搜索型AI系统，如国际象棋程序Deep Blue，通过搜索树验证走棋决策，但无法验证状态评估函数等其他层面的知识。更广泛的AI规划中，许多行动结果具有不确定性，现代AI系统通常忽略了这一点。总体而言，当前AI系统大多无法自我验证知识，依赖人类维护，导致系统脆弱且规模有限。Sutton强调，只有当AI能够自我验证时，才能构建出可靠的大型知识系统。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI应用中的验证问题及其在编码和创新方面的能力

不同观点：
• jbellis认为，早在2001年就有人预见了AI发展中的关键问题，即验证（或现在所称的“评估”）是核心。他指出，大多数从事AI应用工作的人尚未解决这个问题，并推荐关注Hamel Husain以了解最新的发展动态。

• jrvarela56的观点集中在编码代理的应用上。他认为，如果代理不能运行代码，那么它不太可能生成可工作的代码。他进一步指出，除了运行代码，代理还应进行linting、测试、编译、代码审查等过程，这些过程都是人类用来检查软件是否“良好”或正常工作所使用的。如果代理能够应用这些过程来验证其输出，那么我们可以大幅度地自动化大部分工作。他还提到，从产品角度看，如果代理能够通过部署实验并检查用户指标，它最终可能构建出软件产品，但编码部分仍需解决，因为这部分相对容易快速验证。

• a3w则对LLMs（大型语言模型）的创新能力持怀疑态度。他认为，LLMs几乎不能证明任何新颖的想法，只能提供一些已经存在的来源或进行纯数学运算。根据他的观察，到目前为止，这些系统在三年内没有提出任何新颖的想法，形成了“这些系统从未发明任何东西”的悖论。他还提到，符号AI似乎能证明其陈述的一切，但也没有产生新颖的想法。他对神经符号AI能否突破这一局限表示怀疑，认为AI可能最终只是一个末日论的崇拜。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了验证过程在AI应用中的重要性，包括运行代码、linting、测试、编译和代码审查等具体步骤。
• 对LLMs创新能力的质疑和期待，特别是对神经符号AI能否实现突破的讨论。
• 对AI技术发展现状的不同看法和未来预期，包括对AI能否真正实现创新的怀疑和希望。

争议焦点：
• AI在编码和创新方面的实际能力和潜力。
• 验证过程在AI生成内容（如代码）中的应用和重要性。

43933962.article_content:
Verification, The Key to AI
by Rich Sutton
November 15, 2001
It is a bit unseemly for an AI researcher to claim to have a
special insight or plan for how his field should proceed. If he
has such, why doesn't he just pursue it and, if he is right,
exhibit its special fruits? Without denying that, there is still
a role for assessing and analyzing the field as a whole, for
diagnosing the ills that repeatedly plague it, and to suggest
general solutions.
The insight that I would claim to have is that the key to a
successful AI is that it can tell for itself whether or not it
is working correctly. At one level this is a pragmatic issue. If
the AI can't tell for itself whether it is working properly,
then some person has to make that assessment and make any
necessary modifications. An AI that can assess itself may be
able to make the modifications itself.
The Verification Principle:
An AI system can create and maintain knowledge only to the
extent that it can verify that knowledge itself.
Successful verification occurs in all search-based AI systems,
such as planners, game-players, even genetic algorithms. Deep
Blue, for example, produces a score for each of its possible
moves through an extensive search. Its belief that a particular
move is a good one is verified by the search tree that shows its
inevitable production of a good position. These systems don't
have to be told what choices to make; they can tell for
themselves. Image trying to program a chess machine by telling
it what kinds of moves to make in each kind of position. Many
early chess programs were constructed in this way. The problem,
of course, was that there were many different kinds of chess
positions. And the more advice and rules for move selection
given by programmers, the more complex the system became and the
more unexpected interactions there were between rules. The
programs became brittle and unreliable, requiring constant
maintainence, and before long this whole approach lost out to
the "brute force" searchers.
Although search-based planners verify at the move selection
level, they typically cannot verify at other levels. For
example, they often take their state-evaluation scoring function
as given. Even Deep Blue cannot search to the end of the game
and relies on a human-tuned position-scoring function that it
does not assess on its own. A major strength of the champion
backgammon program, TD-Gammon, is that it does assess and
improve its own scoring function.
Another important level at which search-based planners are
almost never subject to verification is that which specifies the
outcomes of the moves, actions, or operators. In games such as
chess with a limited number of legal moves we can easily imagine
programming in the consequences of all of them accurately. But
if we imagine planning in a broader AI context, then many of the
allowed actions will not have their outcomes completely known.
If I take the bagel to Leslie's office, will she be there? How
long will it take to drive to work? Will I finish this report
today? So many of the decisions we take every day have uncertain
and changing effects. Nevertheless, modern AI systems almost
never take this into account. They assume that all the action
models will be entered accurately by hand, even though these may
be most of the knowledge in or ever produced by the system.
Finally, let us make the same point about knowledge in general.
Consider any AI system and the knowledge that it has. It may be
an expert system or a large database like CYC. Or it may be a
robot with knowledge of a building's layout, or knowledge about
how to react in various situations. In all these cases we can
ask if the AI system can verify its own knowledge, or whether it
requires people to intervene to detect errors and unforeseen
interactions, and make corrections. As long as the latter is the
case we will never be able to build really large knowledge
systems. They will always be brittle and unreliable, and limited
in size to what people can monitor and understand themselves.
"Never program anything bigger than your head"
And yet it is overwhelmingly the case that today's AI systems
are
not
able to verify their own knowledge. Large
ontologies and knowledge bases are built that are totally
reliant on human construction and maintenance. "Birds have
wings" they say, but of course they have no way of verifying
this.
43933962.article_summary: Rich Sutton的《验证，AI的关键》一文指出，AI成功的关键在于其能够自我验证是否正常工作。自我验证使得AI系统能够自主评估和修正错误，而不依赖人类干预。文章提出了“验证原则”：AI系统只能在其能够自我验证知识的范围内创建和维护知识。搜索型AI系统，如国际象棋程序Deep Blue，通过搜索树验证走棋决策，但无法验证状态评估函数等其他层面的知识。更广泛的AI规划中，许多行动结果具有不确定性，现代AI系统通常忽略了这一点。总体而言，当前AI系统大多无法自我验证知识，依赖人类维护，导致系统脆弱且规模有限。Sutton强调，只有当AI能够自我验证时，才能构建出可靠的大型知识系统。

data.title: Robotics meets the culinary arts
data.author: gnabgib
data.article_summary: 瑞士和意大利团队合作研发了RoboCake，一种可食用的机器人婚礼蛋糕，展示了机器人食品研究的新进展。这是欧盟资助的RoboFood项目的一部分，由EPFL和意大利技术研究所（IIT）的研究人员与EHL的食品专家和糕点厨师合作完成。RoboCake上装饰着两个完全可食用的机器人泰迪熊，由EPFL的智能系统实验室（LIS）制作，材料包括明胶、糖浆和色素，通过内部气动系统实现运动。IIT研究人员还开发了首款可食用充电电池，由维生素B2、槲皮素、活性炭和巧克力制成，可为蛋糕上的LED蜡烛供电。这些创新不仅旨在创造新的烹饪体验，还试图减少电子废物和食物浪费，并探索在紧急营养和医疗领域的应用。该项目展示了食品与机器人技术结合的潜力，开启了互动和美味的烹饪体验。

Bokeon Kwak, researcher at EPFL's Laboratory of Intelligent Systems and Julien Boutonnet, EHL Senior Lecturer of Practical Arts at EHL - 2025 EPFL/Jamani Caillet - CC-BY-SA 4.0
A Swiss Italian team has created RoboCake, an edible robotic wedding cake that illustrates the advances in robotic food research.
While the idea of creating robots that can be eaten or food that behaves like robots may seem weird, it is a real challenge for the scientific community. As part of the EU-funded RoboFood project, researchers from EPFL and the
Istituto Italiano di Tecnologia
(IIT- Italian Institute of Technology) have collaborated with pastry chefs and food scientists from
EHL in Lausanne
, to marry robotic science and gastronomy. Their project, RoboCake, is being showcased at the Expo 2025 Osaka.
“Robotics and food are two separate worlds,” says Dario Floreano, head of the
Laboratory of Intelligent Systems (LIS)
at EPFL and coordinator of the RoboFood project. “However, merging them offers many advantages, particularly in terms of limiting electronic waste and food waste.” Other applications in the fields of emergency nutrition and health are being considered by scientists. “Edible robots could be used to deliver food to endangered areas, to deliver medicines in innovative ways to people who have difficulty swallowing or to animals, or even to monitor food and its freshness using sensors that can be eaten.
Illustrating robotic food research
Creating edible robots also offers brand new culinary experiences. The RoboCake, a robotic wedding cake, is an innovative demonstration of the progress made by the RoboFood project, which aims to develop a new generation of edible robots and intelligent food.
Edible robotic teddy bears, created by the LIS at EPFL - 2025 EPFL/Jamani Caillet - CC-BY-SA 4.0
The RoboCake features two completely edible robotic teddy bears, created by the LIS at EPFL. “They are made from gelatin, syrup and colorants,” explains Bokeon Kwak, a researcher at LIS.” They are animated by an internal pneumatic system: when air is injected through dedicated pathways, their heads and arms move.”
These dancing bears, which taste like soft, sweet pomegranate gummies, are not the only special feature of the cake. IIT researchers, coordinated by Mario Caironi, have developed the first edible rechargeable battery, made of vitamin B2, quercetin, activated carbon and chocolate, for the gourmet touch. “These batteries, safe for consumption, can be used to light the LED candles on the cake,” explains Valerio Galli, a PhD student at IIT. "The first flavor you get when you eat them is dark chocolate, followed by a surprising tangy kick, due to the edible electrolyte inside, which lasts a few seconds”. These batteries represent a potential solution to reducing electronic waste, which reaches 40 million tons per year.
Edible dark chocolat batteries - 2025 EPFL/Jamani Caillet - CC-BY-SA 4.0
The icing on the cake
To ensure these innovations are both appetizing and safe to eat, the engineers teamed up with food experts and pastry chefs from EHL. “Our challenge was to find the best way to showcase the innovations of our two partners, EPFL and IIT, by adding what we do best: indulgence. This is how the RoboCake was born, a true event pastry cake, meeting the challenge of combining technique, electronics, and taste.” says Julien Boutonnet, EHL Senior Lecturer Practical Arts and France’s top distinction, the Meilleur Ouvrier de France (MOF) award for pastry and candymaking.
“This interdisciplinary collaboration paves the way for interactive and delicious gastronomic experiences reminding us that food is a precious resource and possibly reducing overeating”, says Dario Floreano.
Valerio Galli and Julien Boutonnet - 2025 EPFL/Jamani Caillet - CC-BY-SA 4.0
About the RoboFood project
RoboFood is a 3.5-million-euro four-year research project funded by the European Union. Launched in 2021, it brings together scientists from EPFL, IIT, the University of Bristol and the University of Wageningen. The RoboFood project combines food science and robotics in a radically new way to create edible robots and robotized food for food preservation, emergency nutrition, human and veterinary medicine or new culinary experiences.

data.title: The dark side of account bans
data.author: ponco
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了在线账户被封禁的严重影响，特别是Meta旗下服务如Facebook、Instagram和WhatsApp。作者Maddy Miller是一位Minecraft模组开发者，因遭遇用户骚扰而被人恶意举报，导致所有Meta相关账户被永久封禁。尽管作者尝试通过支持渠道解决问题，但毫无进展，最终通过在社交媒体上求助才幸运地恢复账户。文章指出，失去这些账户不仅影响社交联系，还影响日常生活的诸多方面，如与商家沟通和获取信息。这揭示了现代生活中对大公司在线平台的高度依赖，以及当前账户封禁机制存在的问题，呼吁相关机制需要改进。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Meta平台（包括Facebook和Instagram）的用户体验、账户封禁问题以及数字服务依赖的争议。

不同观点：
• 一些用户（如chrisldgk）分享了自己在Meta平台上遇到的账户封禁问题，尤其是在经过验证后账户仍被封禁，且申诉无效。这揭示了Meta在处理开发者账户和用户申诉方面的不足。
• yellow_lead指出Instagram在处理广告举报时的无效性，认为平台对举报的处理机制存在问题，可能依赖某种阈值机制来决定是否采取行动。
• db48x对比了不同地区餐馆菜单的数字化情况，指出有些地方依赖Instagram展示菜单，而其他地方则使用传统网页或PDF菜单。j1elo对此表示强烈反对，认为这种“数字化狂热”是愚蠢的，忽视了那些不总是携带高端设备的用户。
• dredmorbius和其他用户（如ValdikSS）建议通过法律途径解决问题，如小额索赔法庭，以及联系消费者保护机构和相关政府代表。他们强调组织和行动的重要性，而不是仅仅在社交媒体上抱怨。
• fweimer和stevage讨论了在不同国家（尤其是澳大利亚）通过法律途径解决账户问题的复杂性，并分享了自己或他人通过特殊渠道恢复账户的经历。
• 一些用户（如n4r9和Rebuff5007）对Meta的申诉机制缺失和用户遭遇的不公正对待表示同情，并质疑为什么没有更健全的法律来保护用户免受永久封禁的影响。
• nickdothutton和maxehmookau批评了当前用户举报和平台处理机制的不足，认为普通用户的举报行为往往不可靠，而平台在处理这些举报时缺乏正当程序。
• antonvs分享了自己在Reddit上因发表讽刺言论而被永久封禁的经历，这引发了对言论自由和平台内容审核的进一步讨论。

补充讨论：
• Meta平台的账户封禁和申诉机制问题引发了广泛的关注和不满，用户认为缺乏透明和有效的申诉渠道。

The dark side of account bans
Posted on
May 7, 2025
by
Maddy Miller
In

with tags

Retrospective
In the modern world, online accounts are ubiquitous. You’ve likely got so many that you’d have trouble actually counting them. Almost everything you do requires an account at this point. This wasn’t something I put too much thought into, beyond the mild annoyance of having to sign up to yet another website, until I was recently locked out of all Meta services for nearly two months. This experience was eye opening; it shocked me at how fundamental online platforms owned by companies have actually become to modern life.
What happened
For some background context, I develop a few Minecraft mods that are reasonably popular. If you’re not familiar with game modding communities,
they can be quite toxic sometimes
, with mod developers facing
significant harassment from certain users
. Because we were waiting for mod platforms to stabilise before publishing a final release of
WorldEdit
for a recently released Minecraft update, opting to only publish development builds until we were confident that it wouldn’t suddenly break, I received an anonymous threat.
Threat from an angry user
As threatened, this person attempted to get my online accounts banned. I’m not sure how many they reported, but a few hours later I was notified that my Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp accounts were all permanently banned. I was informed that I would not be able to create a new account, and to never attempt to gain access to a Meta-related system again. These kinds of threats were not new to me; I get hundreds a month. This was also not the first time I lost an account due to an angry user; I lost my PayPal account a few years ago and had to make a new one, due to a similar incident.
I got absolutely nowhere with support. I even paid for my partner’s account to access paid support, in an attempt to get in contact with a real person. I did end up speaking to a few engineers at Meta through connections, either directly or through others, many of which recommended suing Meta to unlock my accounts. This was extra complicated due to me living in Australia, so it’s not something I tried. Eventually, I decided to
make a tweet about it
. Despite the armies of spam bots that immediately inundated my notifications, eventually someone with the ability to unban accounts saw the tweet and unbanned me. The only way I managed to get my account back was sheer luck, likely heavily assisted by the number of people with large follower counts who retweeted my post. If I was not as connected as I am online, I likely would’ve been entirely out of luck.
The dark side of account bans
Now you might be thinking, “Maddy, losing a Facebook account isn’t the end of the world, right?” And yes, that’s what I thought too. I’d always wanted to reduce my reliance on Facebook, and I initially took this as a good excuse to. I was not at all anticipating how hard it would be.
Communication
Facebook is a social network, so the most obvious issue you’d face is losing contact with people on the platform. In Australia, a vast majority of people purely use Facebook Messenger as the way to keep in touch with people. While I’m not happy about it, that’s the current reality of Australian culture. My understanding is that it’s a similar situation with WhatsApp and most of Europe. This meant that not only did I immediately lose access to all of the group chats I was in, I lost my ability to actually contact many people. I don’t save people’s numbers in my contacts because I have everyone on Facebook Messenger, and I never call my friends on the phone.
When I did find alternative ways to contact people, or had other people do it for me, I was met with “Oh I don’t text, do you have Insta or WhatsApp?” If you haven’t noticed the pattern there, both of those platforms are owned by Meta. In Australia, Meta have a near monopoly on the concept of online communication.
Aspects of daily life
A few weeks into my “WorldEdit user”-ordered Meta detox, I tried to organise brunch with a friend. She recommended a few cafes, and I went to look at their menus. To my surprise, I couldn’t access their menus. They were only on Instagram, and it’d force a sign in before showing me the content. This was, of course, concerning. I hadn’t thought much about it beforehand, but so many restaurants and cafes here purely use Instagram (or sometimes Facebook) to host their menus, public holiday trading hours, or other important announcements.
I then went to sell some old PC hardware and asked around for a good marketplace to use. eBay had completely unreasonable fees, and the other ones used in Australia just didn’t have the right demographic to make that sort of sale. If I wanted to successfu

主要讨论点：关于之前讨论的主题链接（https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=33758604）中涉及的观点分析

不同观点：
• 观点一：技术解决方案能否有效解决问题
  - 支持方认为技术创新（如自动化工具、AI等）能够极大改善甚至解决某些社会或行业问题。例如，有人提到AI在医疗诊断中的潜力，认为它可以提高诊断的准确性和效率。
  - 反对方则指出技术往往带来新的问题，比如数据隐私、算法偏见等，这些问题可能比原先的问题更难解决。

• 观点二：技术对就业市场的影响
  - 一些评论者认为，自动化和AI将导致大量工作岗位的流失，特别是在制造业和服务业，这会加剧社会不平等。
  - 另一方则认为技术进步会创造新的就业机会，特别是在科技行业本身，且提高的生产力最终会使社会整体受益。

• 观点三：对先前讨论的引用和扩展
  - 部分评论者引用了之前讨论中的观点，认为需要对技术的影响进行更深入的分析和持续的讨论，以便更好地理解其长远效应。
  - 有人提出，先前的讨论缺乏对伦理问题的关注，建议在未来的讨论中增加对伦理和道德影响的考量。

补充讨论：
• 关于技术发展速度的问题
  - 一些评论者对技术发展的速度表示担忧，认为过快的技术进步可能导致社会、法律和伦理框架无法及时适应。
  - 另一些人则认为技术发展速度是解决当前全球问题（如气候变化、公共卫生等）的必要条件，应该鼓励更快的发展和应用。

• 争议的焦点
  - 主要争议在于技术带来的利益和风险之间的平衡，特别是如何在推动技术进步的同时，尽量减少其负面影响，如失业、隐私问题和伦理困境。
  - 另一个焦点是关于社会对技术发展的准备程度，包括法律法规、教育体系和社会保障制度的适应能力。

总结来看，评论中的讨论围绕技术进步的潜力和风险展开，涉及技术对就业、社会问题的影响以及先前讨论的延续和扩展。争议主要集中在技术发展的利弊权衡和社会适应能力上。

data.title: ALICE detects the conversion of lead into gold at the LHC
data.author: jonbaer
data.article_summary: ALICE合作组在《Physical Review C》发表论文，报告了在大型强子对撞机（LHC）中通过近距未碰撞的铅核产生的电磁相互作用，成功测量了铅转化为金的机制。这一现象类似于中世纪炼金术士梦寐以求的“点金术”。在LHC中，高能铅核产生的强电磁场引发光子与核的相互作用，导致核内部结构振荡，最终排出少量质子和中子，将铅（82个质子）转化为金（79个质子）。研究使用ALICE探测器的零度量能器（ZDC）检测了这一过程，发现LHC当前每秒可产生约89,000个金原子核，但其存在时间极短。在LHC第二轮运行期间，共产生了约860亿个金核，质量约为29皮克。随着LHC亮度的不断提升，第三轮运行产生的金量几乎是第二轮的两倍。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型强子对撞机（LHC）通过实验从铅中生成金，但其商业可行性受到质疑。

不同观点：
• 观点一（成就令人印象深刻）：rubzah认为，LHC在三年内通过实验生成了29皮克的金，尽管每个金原子只存在几纳秒，这仍然是一个非常有趣且令人印象深刻的科学成就。

• 观点二（商业可行性不足）：rubzah指出，尽管实验生成了金，但由于每个金原子存在时间极短，尚不具备商业价值。换句话说，这一科学成果目前无法转化为实际的经济利益。

补充讨论：
• 科学价值 vs. 商业价值：评论暗示了科学实验的成果与其实际应用之间的差距。科学上生成金是一个值得注意的成就，但从商业角度来看，生成金的存在时间太短，无法形成有效的商业应用。

• 时间与稳定性问题：生成的金原子仅存在几纳秒，这意味着在当前技术条件下，无法积累足够稳定数量的金以满足任何商业需求，这也是其商业可行性受到质疑的原因。

争议焦点：
• 科学成就与实际应用之间的矛盾：虽然科学实验取得了进展，但其实际应用和商业价值仍存在较大疑问，这是评论中隐含的争议点。

ALICE detects the conversion of lead into gold at the Large Hadron Collider

ALICE detector. Credit: CERN
In a paper
published
in
Physical Review C
, the ALICE collaboration reports measurements that quantify the transmutation of lead into gold in CERN's Large Hadron Collider (LHC).
Transforming the base metal lead into the precious metal gold was a dream of medieval alchemists. This long-standing quest, known as chrysopoeia, may have been motivated by the observation that dull gray, relatively abundant lead is of a similar density to gold, which has long been coveted for its beautiful color and rarity. It was only much later that it became clear that lead and gold are distinct chemical elements and that chemical methods are powerless to transmute one into the other.
With the dawn of nuclear physics in the 20th century, it was discovered that
heavy elements
could transform into others—either naturally, by radioactive decay—or in the laboratory, under a bombardment of neutrons or protons. Though gold has been artificially produced in this way before, the ALICE collaboration has now measured the transmutation of lead into gold by a new mechanism involving near-miss collisions between
lead nuclei
at the LHC.
Extremely high-energy collisions between lead nuclei at the LHC can create quark–gluon plasma, a hot and dense state of matter that is thought to have filled the universe around a millionth of a second after the Big Bang, giving rise to the matter we now know. However, in the far more frequent interactions where the nuclei just miss each other without "touching," the intense electromagnetic fields surrounding them can induce photon–photon and photon–nucleus interactions that open further avenues of exploration.
The electromagnetic field emanating from a lead nucleus is particularly strong because the nucleus contains 82 protons, each carrying one elementary charge. Moreover, the very high speed at which lead nuclei travel in the LHC (corresponding to 99.999993% of the speed of light) causes the
electromagnetic field
lines to be squashed into a thin pancake, transverse to the direction of motion, producing a short-lived pulse of photons.
Often, this triggers a process called electromagnetic dissociation, whereby a photon interacting with a nucleus can excite oscillations of its internal structure, resulting in the ejection of small numbers of neutrons and protons. To create gold (a nucleus containing 79 protons), three protons must be removed from a lead nucleus in the LHC beams.
An ultra-peripheral collision where the two lead (
208
Pb) ion beams at the LHC pass by close to each other without colliding. In the electromagnetic dissociation process, a photon interacting with a nucleus can excite oscillations of its internal structure and result in the ejection of small numbers of neutrons (two) and protons (three), leaving the gold (
203
Au) nucleus behind. Credit: CERN
"It is impressive to see that our detectors can handle head-on collisions producing thousands of particles, while also being sensitive to collisions where only a few particles are produced at a time, enabling the study of rare electromagnetic 'nuclear transmutation' processes," says Marco Van Leeuwen, ALICE spokesperson.
The ALICE team used the detector's zero degree calorimeters (ZDC) to count the number of photon–nucleus interactions that resulted in the emission of zero, one, two and three protons accompanied by at least one neutron, which are associated with the production of lead, thallium, mercury and gold, respectively.

While less frequent than the creation of thallium or mercury, the results show that the LHC currently produces gold at a maximum rate of about 89,000 nuclei per second from lead–lead collisions at the ALICE collision point. Gold nuclei emerge from the collision with very high energy and hit the LHC beam pipe or collimators at various points downstream, where they immediately fragment into single protons, neutrons and other particles. The gold exists for just a tiny fraction of a second.

-11

• 观点一（成就令人印象深刻）：rubzah认为，LHC在三年内通过实验生成了29皮克的金，尽管每个金原子只存在几纳秒，这仍然是一个非常有趣且令人印象深刻的科学成就。

• 观点二（商业可行性不足）：rubzah指出，尽管实验生成了金，但由于每个金原子存在时间极短，尚不具备商业价值。换句话说，这一科学成果目前无法转化为实际的经济利益。

补充讨论：
• 科学价值 vs. 商业价值：评论暗示了科学实验的成果与其实际应用之间的差距。科学上生成金是一个值得注意的成就，但从商业角度来看，生成金的存在时间太短，无法形成有效的商业应用。

• 时间与稳定性问题：生成的金原子仅存在几纳秒，这意味着在当前技术条件下，无法积累足够稳定数量的金以满足任何商业需求，这也是其商业可行性受到质疑的原因。

争议焦点：
• 科学成就与实际应用之间的矛盾：虽然科学实验取得了进展，但其实际应用和商业价值仍存在较大疑问，这是评论中隐含的争议点。

data.title: Senate passes "cruel" Republican plan to block Wi-Fi hotspots for schoolkids
data.author: croes
data.article_summary: 美国参议院今日投票决定废除联邦通信委员会（FCC）一项向学童提供Wi-Fi热点的计划。该计划旨在通过扩展E-Rate项目帮助没有可靠互联网 access 的学生完成作业。共和党支持者如参议员特德·克鲁兹（Ted Cruz）认为该计划可能让家长失去对孩子上网内容的控制，并可能导致对保守观点的审查。民主党则批评此举短视且残酷，将扩大数字鸿沟，阻碍学生获得必要资源。该计划若要正式废除，还需众议院通过并由总统特朗普签署。FCC主席布兰登·卡尔（Brendan Carr）此前曾反对该计划，认为只有国会能决定是否恢复。

The US Senate today voted along party lines to kill a Federal Communications Commission program to distribute Wi-Fi hotspots to schoolchildren, with Democrats saying the Republican-led vote will make it harder for kids without reliable Internet access to complete their homework.
The Senate approved a Congressional Review Act (CRA)
resolution
to nullify the hotspot rule, which was issued by the Federal Communications Commission
in July 2024
under then-Chairwoman Jessica Rosenworcel. The program would be eliminated if the
House version
passes and President Trump signs the joint resolution of disapproval.
Senator Ted Cruz (R-Texas)
announced
the plan in January, saying the FCC program would "imped[e] parents' ability to decide what their kids see by subsidizing unsupervised access to inappropriate content." He also alleged that the hotspot program would shift control of Internet access from parents to schools and thus "heightens the risk of censoring kids' exposure to conservative viewpoints."
The Rosenworcel FCC's rule expanded E-Rate, a Universal Service Fund program,
allowing
schools and libraries to use E-Rate funding to lend out Wi-Fi hotspots and services that could be used off-premises. The FCC rule was titled, "Addressing the Homework Gap through the E-Rate Program," and the hotspot lending program was
scheduled to begin
in funding year 2025, which
starts in July 2025
.
Markey: “Cruel and shortsighted decision”
Today's Senate vote on the resolution of disapproval was 50–38. There was a 53–47
vote on Tuesday
that allowed the Senate measure to proceed to the final step. Sen. Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.)
said on Tuesday
that "this resolution would prevent millions of students, educators, and families from getting online."
"It would be a disgrace if we deprive those students and their families of this vast resource, of literally life-changing access to a really necessary service that helps them not just now but throughout their futures," Blumenthal said. "We ought to expand Internet access, not constrict it. We ought to be enhancing it, not cutting it off."
Blumenthal pointed out that under a joint resolution of disapproval, the FCC is forbidden to adopt a similar rule in the future. "I have to ask, really? Are schools and teachers crying out to repeal this rule? Really? No, they are not. How does this proposal make any sense for them or for families? For the parents? For the community? It makes no sense," Blumenthal said.
Sen. Edward Markey (D-Mass.)
called
the Republican move "a cruel and shortsighted decision that will widen the digital divide and rob kids of the tools they need to succeed."
FCC’s new chair opposed lending program
The FCC previously distributed Wi-Fi hotspots and other Internet access technology through the Emergency Connectivity Fund (ECF) that was authorized by Congress in 2021. After that program was axed last year, the FCC responded by adapting E-Rate to include hotspot lending.
FCC Chairman Brendan Carr, who was elevated to the agency's top spot by Trump in January, voted against the program last year. Carr said in his
dissent
that only Congress could decide whether to revive the hotspot lending.
"Now that the ECF program has expired, its future is up to Congress," he said at the time. "The legislative branch retains the power to decide whether to continue funding this Wi-Fi loaner program—or not. But Congress has made clear that the FCC's authority to fund this initiative is over."
Overall E-Rate funding is based on demand and
capped
at $4.94 billion per year. Actual spending for E-Rate in 2023 was
$2.48 billion
. E-Rate and other Universal Service Fund programs are paid for through fees imposed on phone companies, which generally pass the cost on to consumers.
The House version of the measure to kill the lending program was introduced by Rep. Russ Fulcher (R-Idaho). "E-Rate was designed to ensure schools and libraries have the connectivity they need to educate and serve their communities, not to create a backdoor entitlement program that stretches beyond the law's clear boundaries," Fulcher
said in February
when he filed the resolution. "The FCC cannot be allowed to unilaterally interpret the law in a way that fits their political agenda. The expansion of this program under the Biden administration was a blatant example of overreach that is not only unlawful but also disregards congressional intent."

Jon Brodkin
Senior IT Reporter
Jon is a Senior IT Reporter for Ars Technica. He covers the telecom industry, Federal Communications Commission rulemakings, broadband consumer affairs, court cases, and government regulation of the tech industry.

data.title: Data manipulations alleged in study that paved way for Microsoft's quantum chip
data.author: EvgeniyZh
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：量子计算研究的现状、挑战及可能的数据操纵问题

不同观点：
• **对量子计算持怀疑态度**：
   - [_heimdall] 认为量子计算目前像是烟雾弹，理论数学复杂且难以验证，怀疑许多研究存在数据操纵或设计缺陷，预测未来还会有更多类似问题曝光。
   - [dreamcompiler] 认为量子计算在实际应用中的工程挑战太大，短期内无法看到投资回报，甚至可能一生都无法见到。
   - [os2warpman] 指出，经过25年的发展，量子计算主要成就只是大量消耗了氦-3，远没有带来实际突破。

• **对研究数据操纵问题的失望和担忧**：
   - [krastanov] 对数据操纵问题感到失望，尤其是在年轻科学家受到影响的情况下，认为这是对科学诚信的打击。
   - [Panoramix] 认为虽然数据挑选和操纵值得质疑，但不一定会完全否定研究结果，可能仍有一定的科学价值，只是结论需要弱化。
   - [sschueller] 感到一些研究人员只是在“扮演”科学家，而不是真正做科学工作，暗示可能存在学术不端行为。

• **为量子计算辩护及解释挑战**：
   - [chermi] 强调微软的数据操纵问题不能否定整个量子计算领域，认为该领域仍在稳步进展。他详细解释了量子计算的难度、多种技术路径的探索以及在学术和工业界之间的文化冲突。
   - [teekert] 提到早在二月份就有学者对微软的研究持怀疑态度，但同时也承认在这样复杂和高风险的领域中，出现问题并不意外。

补充讨论：
• **对量子计算投资和知识产权的看法**：
   - [devwastaken] 认为现代科技的核心是知识产权，即便研究本身不成功，企业仍希望通过知识产权获利，甚至通过占有IP来阻碍他人进展。
   
• **讽刺与幽默**：
   - [russianGuy83829] 和 [trentnix] 以幽默的方式评论此事，认为这可能会成为一个有趣的视频内容或者调侃称世界末日因此推迟。

争议焦点：
• 量子计算是否只是“烟雾弹”，其理论基础和实际应用前景如何。
• 微软在量子计算研究中的数据操纵问题是否严重到影响整个领域的发展。
• 量子计算工程挑战是否能在可预见未来被克服，或是否值得长期投资。

总结：评论中对于量子计算的讨论呈现出明显的两极分化，一部分人对其前景持悲观和怀疑态度，另一部分人则为其辩护，强调其复杂性和潜在价值，同时也指出了研究中的问题和挑战。

data.title: Implementing a Struct of Arrays
data.author: mpweiher
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了如何使用C++26的反射机制实现一个结构体数组（Struct of Arrays, SoA），以替代传统的数组 of 结构体（Array of Structs, AoS）模式，从而提高内存使用效率和性能。文章借鉴了Andrew Kelley在Zig编译器中的优化思路，将原本组合在一起的结构体成员拆分为独立的数组存储。

文章首先解释了Zig语言中如何通过简单的代码修改实现这一优化，然后转向C++26，利用其反射特性来实现类似的`SoaVector<T>`。通过`std::meta::define_aggregate()`函数，文章展示了如何动态生成包含每个非静态数据成员指针的聚合结构体。接着，文章讨论了如何实现`push_back`和`grow`函数来管理动态数组，并确保每个数据成员数组同步增长。

文章的核心在于利用C++26的反射功能简化SoA模式的实现，避免手动处理每个成员的独立数组操作，同时提高代码的可维护性和性能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于面向结构数组（Struct of Arrays, SoA）与面向对象结构（Array of Structs, AoS）性能差异的讨论，以及现代C++的复杂性和元编程（reflection）的应用。

不同观点：
• PessimalDecimal认为，文章起初讨论了列式存储的效率优势，但后来变成了展示C++语言的臃肿和复杂性，暗示现代C++变得过于复杂。
• Dwedit详细分析了SoA和AoS在不同访问模式下的性能差异。他指出，如果按顺序访问对象并查看每个字段，两者性能相近；但如果只访问部分字段，SoA性能更好。而AoS在随机访问所有字段时表现更好。此外，AoS在计算元素地址时涉及乘法运算，而SoA则通过位移运算优化了这一过程。
• gr4vityWall对文章中现代C++的复杂性表示认同，并提到一种在编译时通过宏将AoS转换为SoA以提升性能的方法，但同时质疑这种方法的可读性和“魔法”性质。
• hinkley关注数据结构中的聚合与组合问题，并提到C++中的“handles”分配问题，认为这可能在某些语言中更为重要。
• perihelions展示了如何用Common Lisp实现SoA概念，为有兴趣的读者提供了参考。
• the__alchemist对比了Rust和Zig中的SoA实现，并讨论了在科学计算和GPU编程中的应用，同时对C++文章中的抽象层次表示困惑。

补充讨论：
• monkeyelite提到了“元对象协议”的概念，建议在类定义和实现之间增加一个选择布局和访问方法的阶段。
• mac3n提到了JOVIAL语言中的TABLE结构，可以声明为SERIAL或PARALLEL，与SoA和AoS的讨论相关。
• sph对C++代码中的特定运算符（^^type）表示疑问，显示出对新语法的关注。
• TheHideout简化了讨论，认为文章的核心是利用类似ECS的数组优势来操作结构。
• gpderetta提供了基于模板的SoA实现示例，并质疑反射机制的实际优势。
• jayd16指出文章的核心其实是反射，并认为直接访问字段的假设是荒谬而有趣的。
• gwenzek认为，学习整个Zig语言可能比学习现代C++的元编程更容易。
• adzm对文章中使用的反射运算符（^^）表示赞赏。
• Enthouan认为文章中的实现用C语言会更简单，暗示C++过度复杂化。

争议焦点：现代C++的复杂性与反射机制的实用性。部分评论者认为C++的抽象和元编程增加了不必要的复杂性，而另一些评论者则关注其在特定场景下的优势和应用。

不同观点：

• 有人从历史角度对比，提到亨利·福特希望他的工人能够负担得起他的汽车，而如今贝索斯正用机器人取代工人，质疑未来谁来购买产品。（thisisnotauser）
• 有人指出亚马逊和Ocado在自动化仓库设计上的不同策略，亚马逊是将机器人嵌入人类设计的仓库，而Ocado是人类监督机器人仓库，后者问题相对简单。（philipwhiuk）

  - edu: 建议浮动工具栏可以移动、可折叠，或者放置在画布底部以节省空间。

data.title: How async/await works in Python
data.author: sebg
data.article_summary:
这篇文章简要介绍了Python中的`async`和`await`关键字，以及它们如何使程序变得异步。文章指出，尽管`async`/`await`语法看似同步代码，但实际上允许程序在等待I/O等操作完成时执行其他任务。要理解其工作原理，需了解并发、并行、事件循环、I/O多路复用、异步、协程等概念。

文章强调，即便不使用特殊语言特性也可以编写并发程序，但`async`/`await`使并发编程更加便捷。文章通过构建一个TCP回显服务器，逐步展示从顺序执行到并发版本的演变过程，包括使用OS线程和单线程I/O多路复用与事件循环的方法，最终引入生成器、协程及`async`/`await`。

文章从最简单的顺序服务器代码开始，逐步改进以处理多个客户端，并解释了每个步骤的核心概念和实现方法。

43935452.article_content:
Mark functions as
async
. Call them with
await
. All of a sudden, your program becomes asynchronous – it can do useful things while it waits for other things, such as I/O operations, to complete.
Code written in the
async
/
await
style looks like regular synchronous code but works very differently. To understand how it works, one should be familiar with many non-trivial concepts including concurrency, parallelism, event loops, I/O multiplexing, asynchrony, cooperative multitasking and coroutines. Python's implementation of
async
/
await
adds even more concepts to this list: generators, generator-based coroutines, native coroutines,
yield
and
yield from
. Because of this complexity, many Python programmers that use
async
/
await
do not realize how it actually works. I believe that it should not be the case. The
async
/
await
pattern can be explained in a simple manner if you start from the ground up. And that's what we're going to do today.
Note
: In this post I'm referring to CPython 3.9. Some implementation details will certainly change as CPython evolves. I'll try to keep track of important changes and add update notes.
It's all about concurrency
Computers execute programs sequentially – one instruction after another. But a typical program performs multiple tasks, and it doesn't always make sense to wait for some task to complete before starting the next one. For example, a chess program that waits for a player to make a move should be able to update the clock in the meantime. Such an ability of a program to deal with multiple things simultaneously is what we call
concurrency
. Concurrency doesn't mean that multiple tasks must run at the same physical time. They can run in an interleaved manner: a task runs for some time, then suspends and lets other tasks run, hoping it will get more time in the future. By this mechanism, an OS can run thousands of processes on a machine that has only a few cores. If multiple tasks do run at the same physical time, as in the case of a multi-core machine or a cluster, then we have
parallelism
, a special case of concurrency
[1]
.
It's crucial to realize that you can write concurrent programs without any special support from the language. Suppose you write a program that performs two tasks, each task being represented by a separate function:
def
do_task1
():
# ...
def
do_task2
():
# ...
def
main
():
do_task1
()
do_task2
()
If the tasks are independent, then you can make the program concurrent by decomposing each function into several functions and call the decomposed functions in an interleaved manner, like so:
def
do_task1_part1
():
# ...
def
do_task1_part2
():
# ...
def
do_task2_part1
():
# ...
def
do_task2_part2
():
# ...
def
main
():
do_task1_part1
()
do_task2_part1
()
do_task1_part2
()
do_task2_part2
()
Of course, this is an oversimplified example. The point here is that the language doesn't determine whether you can write concurrent programs or not but may provide features that make concurrent programming more convenient. As we'll learn today,
async
/
await
is just such a feature.
To see how one goes from concurrency to
async
/
await
, we'll write a real-world concurrent program – a TCP echo server that supposed to handle multiple clients simultaneously. We'll start with the simplest, sequential version of the server that is not concurrent. Then we'll make it concurrent using OS threads. After that, we'll see how we can write a concurrent version that runs in a single thread using I/O multiplexing and an event loop. From this point onwards, we'll develop the single-threaded approach by introducing generators, coroutines and, finally,
async
/
await
.

Writing a TCP echo server that handles only one client at a time is straightforward.    - **[quentinp]** 认为文章《a-tale-of-event-loops》帮助他更好地理解了`asyncio`和`Trio`的实现，特别是对“sleep”功能有了更深入的认识。该评论者显然受益于该资源，提升了其对异步编程的认知。

• **[支持多进程替代方案]**：
   - **[incomingpain]** 表示页面无法加载，并直接提出多进程（Multiprocessing）是更好的选择，暗示其可能更倾向于使用多进程而非异步IO。这显示了一种不同的技术倾向，偏好通过多进程来解决问题，而不是依赖异步事件循环。

• **[页面访问问题]**：
   - **[incomingpain]** 提到文章链接无法加载，说明在资源可访问性上可能存在问题，影响了其对原讨论内容的理解和参与。

• **[对异步IO的不同态度]**：
   - **[quentinp]** 对异步IO的细节表现出积极的学习态度，而**[incomingpain]** 则似乎更倾向于多进程方法，表现出对异步IO的怀疑或不感兴趣。这构成了两者在技术路线选择上的潜在争议点。

争议的焦点：事件循环与多进程在Python异步编程中的优劣比较，以及具体使用场景的选择。

The Catholic Church has issued a warning to its clergy in Washington state: Any priest who complies with a new law requiring the reporting of child abuse confessions to authorities will be excommunicated.
The new law, which will take effect on July 27, eliminates the long-standing confidentiality of the confessional, forcing Catholic leaders and lawmakers into a highly charged standoff over religious liberty and child protection.
However, the Archdiocese of Seattle and several bishops argue that the law not only contravenes church doctrine but crosses constitutional lines, while supporters maintain it is a crucial step to protect minors from abuse.
Newsweek
contacted the Archdiocese of Seattle and Washington Governor Bob Ferguson and the three Democratic state senators who sponsored the bill for comment via email and online inquiry forms.
The sun rises behind a stone cross atop the historic Cathedral Basilica of St. Frances of Assisi in Santa Fe, New Mexico.
The sun rises behind a stone cross atop the historic Cathedral Basilica of St. Frances of Assisi in Santa Fe, New Mexico.
Robert Alexander/GETTY
Why It Matters
The issue spotlights the enduring tension between religious freedom and the state's duty to protect children from abuse. By compelling clergy to breach the confessional seal, Washington joins a small group of states stripping traditional confidentiality protections.
The law has triggered a national conversation about the boundaries of church and state, setting a precedent that could have implications for religious practices and privileged communications nationwide. The outcome may influence how other states approach mandated reporting requirements for clergy, especially as constitutional and civil rights groups enter the debate.
What To Know
Washington's new statute requires clergy to report suspected child abuse, explicitly denying exceptions for information revealed during confession.
"Catholic clergy may not violate the seal of confession—or they will be excommunicated from the Church," the Archdiocese of Seattle warned, according to
Fox News
.
The Catholic Church's canon law regards breaking the confessional seal as a grave offense: "A confessor who directly violates the seal of confession incurs an automatic excommunication reserved to the Apostolic See."
The U.S.
Department of Justice
said it is investigating whether the law infringes on First Amendment religious protections.
Voting by the College of Cardinals to select the next pope is set to begin Wednesday, following the
death of Pope Francis on April 21.
Francis' funeral took place
at the Vatican on April 26
, with dignitaries including U.S. President
Donald Trump
, Ukrainian President
Volodymyr Zelensky
and
Prince William
in attendance.
The current favorites are Italian Cardinal Pietro Parolin and Filipino Cardinal Luis Antonio Tagle, according to U.K.-based bookmaker William Hill, with odds of 12/5 (29.4 percent) and 3/1 (25 percent), respectively.
On April 2, Trump sparked controversy by sharing an AI-generated image that
depicted him as the pope
on his Truth Social website.
What People Are Saying
Speaking to
Newsweek
Professor Michele Dillon, an expert on Catholicism at the University of New Hampshire, said:
"This is highly controversial because it directly challenges a core element of the Catholic faith...For the government to require priests to report any instance of sex abuse that they learn about through the sacrament of confession would directly violate the core of the sacrament and its significance in Catholics' lives. The Church has made significant strides in recent years to safeguard children from sex abuse, and so it's unfortunate that the controversy stoked by the Washington State law – and the church's opposition to it based on core theological belief and practice – may erroneously convey to people who are not familiar with the full meaning of the sacrament that the Church is opposing the requirement simply to evade dealing with the issue of
